best_field_traits: Taxonomy caution: this project uses D. lindheimeri; many FNA/USDA sources treat the same concept as D. acuminatum var./subsp. lindheimeri. Do NOT create a duplicate card.
Basal rosette distinct in suitable season; upper stem leaves commonly 4–9 cm by 4–8 mm, often yellowish green.
Leaf surfaces and sheaths generally glabrous or sparsely hairy; conspicuous long papillose-based cilia near the blade base.
Ligule of hairs, often several millimeters long; compare actual collar, not just the nearby blade-margin cilia.
Open primary panicle about 3.5–7 cm; tiny often obtuse, obovoid spikelets about 1.3–1.6 mm.
Late-season stems develop many small leafy branch clusters (fascicles) and reduced secondary flowering heads.
crew_field_check: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
2. On living same-plant shoot find spring basal rosette and compare early spring versus late-season leafy secondary shoots.
3. Open the collar: photograph true hair-fringe ligule separately from hairs at the blade base, with mm scale.

4. Measure at least three mature ripe SPIKELETS with 1-mm ruler; size categories ~1.3–1.6 lindheimeri, 2.1–3.2 commutatum, ~2.9–4 oligosanthes, ~3–3.5 pedicellatum, but overlapping ranges prohibit pure size-only identification.
5. If rosette/collar/leaf base or mature spikelet dimensions unavailable, record Dichanthelium sp. and a source-determined tentative species.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Lindheimer's panicgrass — evidence limits and next checks
steps: 1. Photo 1 is an existing provisional CC BY-NC field/habitat image; it does NOT isolate a mature measured spikelet, true ligule, basal cilia or connected seasonal rosette. It is NOT a cleared public photo under the current CC0/CC BY/CC BY-SA policy.
2. Photo 2 is a PUBLIC-DOMAIN HISTORICAL ILLUSTRATION under an older Panicum lindheimeri name concept, NOT a photograph of the present plant; do not present it as pixel-verified modern anatomy.

3. The previously displayed Cody Stricker photos 632023937 and 632024018 were determined to depict D. pedicellatum, not D. lindheimeri, and were removed. They must NOT be featured or cited as Lindheimer diagnostic evidence.
4. Find a source-vouchered same-plant flowering shoot, rooted spring rosette and later branching growth; retain individual season/date labels.
5. At 10–20× document true inner ligule with 1-mm ruler, basal blade-margin cilia, and three ripe 1.3–1.7-mm spikelets; separate lower/upper glumes and both florets.
6. Compare species-authenticated D. commutatum, D. oligosanthes and D. pedicellatum at matched scales before confirming a difficult local plant.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Without a source-vouchered measured 1.3–1.7-mm ripe spikelet plus real ligule and basal blade cilia, teach Dichanthelium sp./Lindheimer candidate only.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Two current image records only: one CC BY-NC provisional field photo and one historical public-domain illustration. The misattributed D. pedicellatum photos were removed; do not revive their stale photo indices. No new images or anatomy arrows; public Pages not verified.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.details: Lindheimer's panicgrass has exceptionally small, blunt oval mature spikelets; the 2015 revision reports 1.3–1.7 mm long. An open spring panicle and perennial rosette habit support the ID but are not species-specific. The only existing field photograph is not a measured spikelet close-up, and the historical drawing is not a real plant photograph.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · EXAMINE BASAL BLADE HAIRS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Long cilia often at the blade base
field_id_short_tiles.details: On a source-confirmed spring shoot, inspect the base of the stem leaf for conspicuous papillose-based marginal hairs. The 2015 taxonomic revision identifies basal blade-margin cilia as an important character in D. lindheimeri. The upper sheath can be nearly smooth; a few hairs alone are not a species diagnosis. Current gallery pixels do not verify these hairs.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · FIND THE TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Inner hair fringe; published ranges differ
field_id_short_tiles.details: At the INSIDE blade–sheath junction, inspect the true ligule separately from blade-edge cilia. A 2015 species-level revision reports roughly 2.0–3.2-mm ligule hairs, while an older USDA treatment describes a white hair ring about 4–5 mm. Preserve the source disagreement rather than teaching a hard cutoff; take a 1-mm scaled collar photograph before adding an arrow.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE RANGE DISAGREEMENT; TRUE COLLAR PHOTO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · DISSECT LOWER AND UPPER GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.details: The 2015 species-level revision reports a short LOWER glume about 0.3–0.6 mm, generally no more than one-third the spikelet. The UPPER glume approaches the fertile floret length. Backlight and measure both from one mature spikelet; do not place glume-vein arrows on the current habitat image or historic illustration as if photographed anatomy were resolved.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED LOWER GLUME; MEASURED DISSECTION MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · FIND THE STERILE AND FERTILE FLORETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: One lower sterile and one upper fertile; awnless
field_id_short_tiles.details: Each small spikelet contains a lower sterile floret and upper seed-bearing fertile floret. In the broader D. acuminatum treatment the hardened fertile upper floret is roughly 1.1–1.7 mm long; this is COMPLEX-LEVEL reference, not an independent measurement from this card's photographs. Separate the thin sterile lemma from the hardened fertile lemma/palea; no long lemma awns are expected.
field_id_short_tiles.status: BROADER COMPLEX MEASUREMENT; SPECIES DISSECTION MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · KEEP THE TAXON AND PHOTOS STRAIGHT
field_id_short_tiles.short: Not pedicellatum; compare actual spikelet sizes
field_id_short_tiles.details: D. oligosanthes (about 2.9–4 mm) and D. pedicellatum (about 3–3.5 mm) have substantially larger mature spikelets; D. commutatum overlaps toward the smaller end and needs leaf-base/collar examination. Older D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri is a historical rank treatment, NOT a new species to install. Two Cody Stricker photos previously imported under this card were discovered to be D. pedicellatum and removed; NEVER use them as Lindheimer evidence.
field_id_short_tiles.status: MISATTRIBUTED PHOTO HOLD PRESERVED; MATCHED SPECIES PHOTOS MISSING
